book: The Zohar — Book of Splendour, Selections

1: In the beginning of the mind of the King, a point shone forth, and that point was the beginning of all things, and it expanded into a palace, and within the palace all the worlds were hidden, and from it the light broke forth like one candle kindling another.
[Zohar I, 15b — The hidden and the revealed]

There is a garment for every word of Torah, and within the garment a body, and within the body a soul, and within the soul a soul of souls. The wise see the soul; the simple see only the garment, and even the garment of the Torah is glory.
[Zohar I, 20b — The moon and her light]
The moon has no light of her own, yet she is never dark, for she is turned always toward the sun. So is the community of Israel: it shines only with a borrowed light, and is never without it.
2: When the King made the worlds, sparks of His light fell and were scattered like sparks from a hammer. And He made man to gather them up again: every good deed lifts a spark home. This is the meaning of the commandment, and this is the labour of the world.

Rabbi Yehuda said: All gates are closed save the gate of tears. There is no door that tears cannot open, for the King counts them and keeps them in His storehouse, and answers them before all other prayers.

The Torah is one, though it is read as seventy faces. Turn it and turn it, for everything is in it; and the last secret is the same as the first, for the Holy One is one, and His word is one, though we see it in many colours.
3: Before the soul descends into the world it is shown all that it will do, and it weeps, saying: Master of the world, why send me into a body of dust? And the answer comes: Whether you will or not, you shall go; and the going is your mending, and your mending is My delight.

He who hides his candle from his neighbour robs the whole house of light. For the candle was given for the house, and the house for the candle, and he who shares his light finds it multiplied, not diminished.
[Zohar III, 271b — The world to come begins now]
Said Rabbi Shimon: The world to come is not built in a day that has not dawned; it is built now, in this one, by every act of love. The meek heart is the first stone of it, and it is already laid.
